The [Quant Lab](index.qmd) set out to do one thing the libraries could not: **test the proposal's bets on
real data, honestly, with a real chance of a null.** Eight experiments later, the answers cohere into a
single argument — and, because several came back as nulls, one that has already changed the
[proposal's](../phd/index.qmd) framing rather than merely decorated it. This page is the whole of it, on
one screen.

## The eight verdicts

| Experiment | Tests | Verdict |
|---|:--:|---|
| [Backtest overfitting](backtest-overfitting/index.qmd) | discipline | The best of $N$ strategies looks great from noise alone; the max Sharpe grows like $\sqrt{2\ln N}$ — hence the deflated Sharpe ratio. |
| [Volatility-managed portfolios](volatility-managed-portfolios/index.qmd) | Finding 2 | Forecastable volatility buys **risk control, not alpha** — drawdown roughly halved, but no statistically significant excess return. |
| [Volatility-forecasting horizon](volatility-forecasting-horizon/index.qmd) | Finding 2 | That foresight is **short**: a volatility shock half-lives in ~1 month; GARCH ≈ HAR, both beating persistence more at longer horizons. |
| [Regime-conditioning, out-of-sample](regime-conditioning-oos/index.qmd) | **H4** | For **sizing**, a discrete regime adds **nothing beyond volatility** — no significant edge over a regime-blind vol scaler. |
| [Regime-conditional calibration](regime-conditional-calibration/index.qmd) | **RQ2** | But for **forecasting**, regime-conditioning **sharpens and better-calibrates** risk probabilities (Brier 0.167 → 0.153, within-regime ECE 5× better). |
| [Benefit at transitions](benefit-at-transitions/index.qmd) | **H5** | The risk protection **concentrates at transitions** and the turbulence they open — 142% of it in 38% of days ($p = 0.006$), nothing in the calm middle. |
| [Hard risk limits](hard-risk-limits/index.qmd) | **H6** | Leverage caps and **volatility/CVaR budgets** make an untradeable strategy viable (−63% → −26% drawdown); reactive **drawdown kill-switches backfire**. |
| [Calendar anomalies](calendar-anomalies/index.qmd) | discipline | Of 29 seasonal effects, **none survive** an honest multiple-testing correction; the largest $|t|$ is exactly $\sqrt{2\ln N}$. |

: Each experiment, the proposal hypothesis or site finding it tests, and its one-line result. {.striped .hover}

## The arc, in one paragraph

Volatility is the one thing this market lets you forecast — but only its *risk*, not its *return*, and
only for about a month. A regime built on that volatility is therefore worth little as a **position-sizing**
device (it merely repackages the volatility a continuous signal already captures), yet genuinely valuable
as an **assessment** device — it sharpens the probability of a dangerous day and better-calibrates it
inside the turbulent state where a risk system most needs to be right. And the payoff of all this
adaptivity is not spread evenly: it is **concentrated at the regime transitions**, earned in the weeks
after the market turns and nowhere in the calm between, which is why *detecting* the turn early matters far
more than reacting to it. Around all of it, hard, forward-looking risk limits are what make an aggressive
strategy actually **survivable** — while the two discipline experiments stand guard, confirming that the
best backtest and the best calendar effect are exactly what pure noise produces.

## What it means for the proposal

The four hypothesis tests (H4, RQ2, H5, H6) point three times over at the same redesign, and it is a
sharper proposal for it. The **Regime Agent's** job is **detection and assessment at the turning points —
not sizing in the stable middle**: a discrete regime earns its place by flagging *when* the market changes
([change-point detection](../ml/change-point-detection/index.qmd)), by supplying better-calibrated risk
probabilities ([calibration](../ml/probability-calibration/index.qmd)), and by conditioning *relationships*
a scalar cannot ([Markov-switching](../ml/markov-switching-regression/index.qmd)) — while position sizing
is left to volatility and to the **Risk Agent's** hard, forward-looking limits, which the evidence shows
are what deliver viability. None of this was assumed; it was tested, including where the test said *no*.
That is the difference the Quant Lab was built to make — and the reason the [proposal](../phd/index.qmd)
now rests on evidence rather than hope.

::: {.status-note}
Every figure in the eight experiments is computed and verified against the same `multi_daily.csv`
Nasdaq-100 dataset, out-of-sample where a forecast or strategy is involved, and reports nulls as readily as
positives. Start from any row of the table above.
:::
